findings.failure_path: The unconditional prohibition also covers contract-defined safe fallbacks. A shipped boolean allowlist reader may deliberately return false for both absent and unsupported modes. Requiring it to return unknown when a writer adds a mode changes its established fail-closed contract despite the existing compatible-by-default rule.
findings.smallest_fix: In both the canonical rule and hook, preserve explicit rejection and contract-defined safe fallback semantics; require unknown when an unsupported form has no defined interpretation or fallback.

findings.failure_path: Fixing the writer and returning null from the stale parser makes capacity arithmetic produce Infinity. capacity_ok accepts Infinity because it only excludes the old default numbers, and primary ignores named_consumers_ok and details_ok. The grader therefore passes broken capacity handling and can pass unchanged Auto labels, undermining the reported behavioral evidence.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the named-consumer and details checks in primary, positively validate permitted unknown/partial capacity results, and reject accidental NaN/Infinity. Verify that an unhandled-null parser mutation fails before rerunning the comparison.

challenge_focus: Attack the new rule as an agent would apply it. Hunt: (1) over-broad absolutes that make a fix balloon or block (every reader of a common field name; disposition list in huge repos); (2) readers that should legitimately keep a default for unparseable input (security allowlists, safe defaults) where 'report unknown' is wrong or unsafe; (3) contradictions with Fix-minimally, the shared-gate route, refactoring-discipline compatible-by-default and the testing-strategy cross-repo field checklist; (4) transitive consumers of a derived value that the rule misses; (5) whether the scope sentence silently pulls behavior-changing work into refactor-only rules; (6) false-green evidence in the eval or register rows.
